name: Kongo Christianity (Afonso-era Catholic state cult)

dating.dating_summary: Baptism of Nzinga a Nkuwu (as João I) 3 May 1491 was a MISSIONIZATION event that did not durably hold (he apostatized c. 1494-95); durable STATE_ADOPTION dates to Afonso I's reign from 1509, combined with documented terminological/visual SYNCRETISM continuing through the 17th century Kimpasi society and the Cardoso 1624 catechism.

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: Elaborate hybrid crucifixes and other Kongo Christian visual-art objects survive from the 16th-18th centuries (Cécile Fromont, The Art of Conversion, UNC Press 2014) but this research pass did not verify a specific earliest-dated excavated example.

earliest_written_attestation.note: Baptism of Nzinga a Nkuwu as João I, 3 May 1491, with son Nzinga a Mbemba (later Afonso I) and court officials baptized alongside him.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: The 1624 Kikongo catechism produced under Jesuit Mateus Cardoso, translated by named Kongo "best masters of the church," is the earliest surviving full catechism (a now-lost 1557 Carmelite catechism preceded it but its exact wording is not independently verifiable). Also: John K. Thornton, Afonso I Mvemba a Nzinga, King of Kongo: His Life and Correspondence (Hackett, 2020) — Afonso I's own surviving letters, most famously a series from 1526 protesting the Atlantic slave trade to King João III of Portugal.

tradition_internal_claim.note: N/A — an imported tradition with a documented, non-legendary founding sequence (unlike most traditions in this batch).

notes: Afonso I (r. 1509-1542) declared traditional "idol" worship illegal, burned at least one traditional shrine, built churches/schools, used Christian primogeniture doctrine to strengthen his own succession claim. Cécile Fromont documents the pre-existing Kongo dikenga/yowa cross-shaped cosmogram (four moments of the sun: kala/tukula/luvemba/musoni) as a genuine point of visual-cosmological convergence with the Christian crucifix, not a one-sided imposition.
